title: Provide a lightbox UI for images attached to issues
body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested on a next instance)

### About your usage of Forgejo

I am a regular Codeberg user, which includes working with issues. When developing GUI applications, images in issues are often needed to illustrate certain points, and a smooth UX for images makes that a lot easier.

### Problem description

Currently, when issues (or other tickets, such as PRs) have image attachments, clicking on the thumbnail opens the image in a new tab. If there are multiple image attachments to the same issue, even in the same comment, clicking through them is a bit of a hassle at the moment: click one, close the tab, click the next etc.

From a user perspective, a good solution would be a lightbox UI (for example, similar to the one at https://simplelightbox.com/): Clicking on an image attachment opens the full-size image in the lightbox, which allows cycling through consecutive images by clicking the Previous/Next buttons or swiping left/right. Another button closes the lightbox.

This UX is quite standard for similar use cases such as classified portals, discussion forums and the like. GitLab recently introduced the feature ([issue 377398](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/377398), [merge request 203609](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/203609)).

### Potential workarounds

title: problem:
body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested locally with the latest development version)

### About your usage of Forgejo

We are a medium sized company and use multiple Forgejo instances to host git repositories across multiple teams. I am the owner / provider of the service.

### Problem description

Users have a situation where they develop a library or core of an application in a repository. Then other repositories exist depending on the core repo (its source code). The later are the actual application. All repositories are private. We use Forgejo Actions to trigger image builds. In simple cases only a single repository is needed and the temporary default workflow token can be used to get the repo contents. Since in my opinion this is quite a good approach for handling credentials i'd like to be able to use a similar mechanism to get another repos contents.

I spend some time thinking about how I as a user would like to use such a feature. I feel like it would be a repository setting in the core repository where an owner may configure what other repos are allowed to see the core repo contents within a workflow run. These are just my thoughts. I am aware that this is likely is a major change in data modelling and API. I am happy here about other thoughts.

### Potential workarounds

In the case where build dependencies are contained in a private repo I found [this](https://code.forgejo.org/actions/checkout#checkout-multiple-repos-private) reference from the runner documentation. This surely works but seams to depend on secrets which is longer lived the the internally manged token. Furthermore we would need some user to create the token which should not be a human user account that might leave the instance at some point.

I read though his [issue](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/issues/1712) which seams to discuss some great improvements to Forgejo! Apparently organization tokens are on there way. This would somewhat improve my previous statement but I still prefer the "Internal Token" approach. It's limited lifetime is quite elegant.

### Forgejo Version

17.0.1-rootless

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

DB: sqlite
Depliyemnt: codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo (k8s)
